Services as a Layer

Why ticket logic lives in its own file, separate from the controller that calls it.

Laravel got you comfortable with routes → controllers → models. This project adds a layer Laravel never pushed you toward: services, sitting between controllers and data. getAllTickets in the controller (previous slide) doesn't touch the ticket data itself — it calls ticketService.getAllTickets() and returns whatever comes back.

// Figure 1.8: the ticket service (src/services/ticket.service.js, excerpt)
let tickets = [
  { id: 1, subject: 'Cannot log in', description: 'Password reset email never arrives', status: 'open' },
  { id: 2, subject: 'Invoice discrepancy', description: 'Charged twice for March', status: 'open' },
];
let nextId = tickets.length + 1;

export const getAllTickets = async () => tickets;

export const getTicketById = async (id) => tickets.find((ticket) => ticket.id === id);

export const createTicket = async ({ subject, description }) => {
  const ticket = { id: nextId++, subject, description, status: 'open' };
  tickets.push(ticket);
  return ticket;
};

Why bother, when the controller could just as easily hold this logic itself? Two reasons, and they only get more valuable as the API grows over the coming weeks:

  • The controller's job stays "translate HTTP ↔ data." It reads the request, calls a service, shapes a response. It never needs to know how tickets are fetched or stored.
  • That "how" can change without touching the controller at all. Right now ticket.service.js is an in-memory array. From Week 2 onward it becomes real Prisma/MySQL queries — and because the controller only ever called ticketService.getAllTickets(), not touched the array directly, not a single line in ticket.controller.js needs to change when that happens.

This is exactly why every function here is already declared async, even though none of them currently await anything — a real database call will need to be awaited, and making that change later shouldn't require changing every caller's shape too. Laravel doesn't force this split because Eloquent models already give you a query-building layer separate from the controller; without an ORM (yet), Express gives you nothing there for free, so this project adds the layer by hand.
